sources.entry: Photoview - Simple and user-friendly photo gallery for personal servers. It is made for photographers and aims to provide an easy and fast way to navigate directories, with thousands of high resolution photos. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Photoview is a self-hosted photo gallery that maps server directories to albums, aimed at photographers with large libraries of high-resolution and RAW photos.
summary.what_it_does: Photoview scans a directory on the server's file system for photos and videos and generates thumbnails so browsing is quick. Directories are presented as albums in the same structure as on disk. Users are created with a filesystem path, so each user only sees photos within that path. Albums and individual media can be shared through public links, optionally password protected. It supports RAW formats and EXIF parsing, plus video with automatic web optimization. It also detects faces and groups photos of the same person.
use_cases: self-hosted photo gallery for a home server
browsing RAW photo collections over a network
sharing photo albums with family via public links
multi-user access to a shared photo archive
organizing photos by folder structure on a file server
how_to_run: Download the docker-compose example folder from the repository to your server
Rename the example files (.env, docker-compose.yml, Makefile) by removing 'example' from their names
Edit .env and docker-compose.yml per the comments to match your setup
Run 'make readable' (or the equivalent commands) so the media folders are readable by others
Run 'make all' to start the server
Open the site, complete the initial setup wizard, and run 'Scan All' from Settings
notable: Directories on disk map directly to albums, so the filesystem stays the source of truth
Optional hardware-accelerated video transcoding (qsv, vaapi, nvenc)
Public share links for albums and media, with optional password protection
Face recognition groups photos by person
caveats: Docker Compose is the primary supported platform; Portainer and similar abstraction layers are not supported
SQLite has the lowest performance and no scalability; PostgreSQL 18 is recommended for the best performance
Hardware acceleration was verified only with qsv on Intel chips
The maintainers recommend securing the instance with additional layers (firewall, VPN, reverse proxy) before exposing it publicly
